claim: Protein-correlation-profiling (PCP), in combination with quantitative proteomics, has emerged as a high-throughput method for the rapid identification of dynamic protein complexes in native conditions.
source: Protein-correlation-profiling (PCP), in combination with quantitative proteomics, has emerged as a high-throughput method for the rapid identification of dynamic protein complexes in native conditions.
evidence: This is a general statement about the field supported by the context of the manuscript and established scientific knowledge.

claim: Characterization of the membrane interactome has lagged due to the necessary use of detergents to maintain protein solubility.
source: While PCP has been successfully applied to soluble proteomes, characterization of the membrane interactome has lagged, partly due to the necessary use of detergents to maintain protein solubility.
evidence: This statement is supported by the context and rationale provided in the manuscript.

claim: The peptidisc is a 'one-size fits all' membrane mimetic.
source: Here, we apply the peptidisc, a 'one-size fits all' membrane mimetic, for the capture of the Escherichia coli cell envelope proteome and its high-resolution fractionation in the absence of detergent.
evidence: This is a characterization of the peptidisc technology used in the study.

claim: Analysis of the SILAC-labeled peptidisc library via PCP allows generation of over 4900 possible binary interactions out of >700,000 random associations.
source: Analysis of the SILAC-labeled peptidisc library via PCP allows generation of over 4900 possible binary interactions out of >700,000 random associations.
evidence: This is a primary finding directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The SecY translocon, the Bam complex and the MetNI transporter are well-characterized membrane protein systems.
source: Using well-characterized membrane protein systems such as the SecY translocon, the Bam complex and the MetNI transporter, we demonstrate that our dataset is a useful resource for identifying transient and surprisingly novel protein interactions.
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific knowledge about these protein systems.

claim: A trans-periplasmic supercomplex comprises subunits of the Bam and Sec machineries, including membrane-bound chaperones YfgM and PpiD.
source: For example, we discover a trans-periplasmic supercomplex comprising subunits of the Bam and Sec machineries, including membrane-bound chaperones YfgM and PpiD.
evidence: This is a novel finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: RcsF and OmpA are bona fide interactors of BamA.
source: We identify RcsF and OmpA as bone fide interactors of BamA, and we show that MetQ association with the ABC transporter MetNI depends on its N-terminal lipid anchor.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: MetQ association with the ABC transporter MetNI depends on its N-terminal lipid anchor.
source: We identify RcsF and OmpA as bone fide interactors of BamA, and we show that MetQ association with the ABC transporter MetNI depends on its N-terminal lipid anchor.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: NlpA is a novel interactor of MetNI complex.
source: We also discover NlpA as a novel interactor of MetNI complex.
evidence: This is a novel finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Most of the interactions discovered are largely undetected by standard detergent-based purification.
source: Most of these interactions are largely undetected by standard detergent-based purification.
evidence: This is supported by comparative experimental data between detergent and peptidisc methods.

claim: The peptidisc workflow is emerging as a promising novel approach to characterize membrane protein interactions under native expression conditions and without genetic manipulation.
source: Together, the peptidisc workflow applied to the proteomic field is emerging as a promising novel approach to characterize membrane protein interactions under native expression conditions and without genetic manipulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results and data presented in the study.

claim: Affinity purification coupled to identification by mass spectrometry (AP/MS) has been used to characterize protein-protein interaction networks.
source: Characterizing protein-protein interaction networks (the interactome) has traditionally been accomplished by methods such as affinity purification coupled to identification by mass spectrometry (AP/MS) (Arifuzzaman et al., 2006; Hu et al., 2009; Babu et al., 2012; Babu et al., 2018), protein fragment complementation assays (Rochette et al., 2015; Tarassov et al., 2008), or yeast two-hybrid screening (Y2H) (Rajagopala et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Protein fragment complementation assays have been used to characterize protein-protein interaction networks.
source: Characterizing protein-protein interaction networks (the interactome) has traditionally been accomplished by methods such as affinity purification coupled to identification by mass spectrometry (AP/MS) (Arifuzzaman et al., 2006; Hu et al., 2009; Babu et al., 2012; Babu et al., 2018), protein fragment complementation assays (Rochette et al., 2015; Tarassov et al., 2008), or yeast two-hybrid screening (Y2H) (Rajagopala et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Yeast two-hybrid screening (Y2H) has been used to characterize protein-protein interaction networks.
source: Characterizing protein-protein interaction networks (the interactome) has traditionally been accomplished by methods such as affinity purification coupled to identification by mass spectrometry (AP/MS) (Arifuzzaman et al., 2006; Hu et al., 2009; Babu et al., 2012; Babu et al., 2018), protein fragment complementation assays (Rochette et al., 2015; Tarassov et al., 2008), or yeast two-hybrid screening (Y2H) (Rajagopala et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Traditional interactome methods are limited in scope by poor scalability because bait proteins must be independently tagged.
source: While high-throughput, these methods are quite often limited in their scope by poor scalability because bait proteins must be independently tagged.
evidence: This is a known limitation of traditional methods supported by scientific knowledge.

claim: Addition of tags can have uncontrolled effects on proteins such as disrupting binding sites, altering localization, and stability.
source: The addition of these tags can also have uncontrolled effects on proteins such as disrupting binding sites, altering localization, stability, and thereby the accurate prediction of the interactome.
evidence: This is a known limitation of tagging methods supported by scientific knowledge.

claim: Co-fractionation methods such as protein-correlation-profiling (PCP) are emerging as an attractive alternative to identify protein complexes under native expression conditions.
source: Co-fractionation methods, such as protein-correlation-profiling (PCP) in combination with quantitative proteomics methods, such as label-free quantitation (LFQ) or stable isotope labeling of amino acids in cell culture (SILAC), are therefore emerging as an attractive alternative to identify protein complexes under native expression conditions and without genetic manipulation (Kristensen et al., 2012; Scott et al., 2017; Havugimana et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: PCP can generate thousands of potential interactions in a single experiment.
source: This method can generate thousands of potential interactions in a single experiment, and incorporation of SILAC multiplexing allows simultaneous comparison of multiple states of the interactome (Kristensen et al., 2012; Scott et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Incorporation of SILAC multiplexing allows simultaneous comparison of multiple states of the interactome.
source: This method can generate thousands of potential interactions in a single experiment, and incorporation of SILAC multiplexing allows simultaneous comparison of multiple states of the interactome (Kristensen et al., 2012; Scott et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Characterization of the membrane proteome has lagged due to the hydrophobic nature of membrane proteins and their sequestration in the lipid membrane.
source: While co-fractionation has been successfully applied to soluble proteomes, characterization of the membrane proteome has lagged. This is largely due to the hydrophobic nature of membrane proteins and their sequestration in the lipid membrane.
evidence: This is a known challenge in the field supported by scientific knowledge.

claim: It is necessary to solubilize the lipid bilayer with the aid of detergents or amphipathic co-polymers such as styrene maleic acid (SMA) to extract the water-insoluble proteome.
source: To extract this water-insoluble proteome, it is necessary to solubilize the lipid bilayer with the aid of detergents or amphipathic co-polymers such as styrene maleic acid (SMA) (Dörr et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and represents established methodology.

claim: Even the mildest detergents tend to decrease protein stability while increasing protein aggregation.
source: However, even the mildest detergents tend to decrease protein stability while increasing protein aggregation (Yang et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Prolonged exposure to detergents tends to delipidate proteins and alter their conformation, which can have confounding effects on membrane protein complex stability.
source: In fact, prolonged exposure to those detergents tends to delipidate proteins and alter their conformation, which can have confounding effects on membrane protein complex stability.
evidence: This is a known effect of detergents supported by scientific knowledge and the context of the manuscript.

claim: Micelles of detergent must be removed from all samples before analysis by mass spectrometry, which often decreases protein identification.
source: As an additional drawback, micelles of detergent must be removed from all samples before analysis by mass spectrometry, which often decreases protein identification (Yeung and Stanley, 2010; Bechara et al., 2015; Bao et al., 2013; Yang et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: The peptidisc is formed when multiple copies of the 4.5 kDa amphipathic scaffold NSPr wrap around the solubilized membrane proteins.
source: The peptidisc is formed when multiple copies of the 4.5 kDa amphipathic scaffold NSPr (also called Peptidisc peptide) wrap around the solubilized membrane proteins.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of peptidisc formation based on the authors' previous work.

claim: Reconstitution of peptidisc occurs spontaneously upon removal of detergent, incorporating both endogenous lipids and solubilized membrane proteins into detergent-free particles.
source: Reconstitution occurs spontaneously upon removal of detergent, incorporating both endogenous lipids and solubilized membrane proteins into detergent-free particles.
evidence: This describes the peptidisc reconstitution process based on the authors' previous work.

claim: The number of peptidisc scaffolds adapts to fit the diameter of the protein target without bias toward large protein complexes.
source: The number of scaffolds adapts to fit the diameter of the protein target without bias toward large protein complexes.
evidence: This is a characteristic of the peptidisc technology based on the authors' previous work.

claim: Peptidisc particles are stable, free of detergent effects, and soluble in aqueous solution.
source: The end result is peptidisc particles that are stable, free of detergent effects, and soluble in aqueous solution (Carlson et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The peptidisc is able to stabilize both inner and outer membrane proteins of Escherichia coli.
source: Our previous work has shown that the peptidisc is able to stabilize both inner and outer membrane proteins of Escherichia coli.
evidence: This statement refers to findings from the authors' previous work.

claim: The membrane proteome trapped in the peptidisc library is water-soluble and stable during prolonged incubations.
source: The membrane proteome trapped in the peptidisc library is water-soluble and stable during prolonged incubations.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by experimental observations.

claim: 1209 unique proteins were identified and quantified from the peptidisc library, of which 591 are predicted to be directly membrane integrated.
source: When the peptidisc library from the raw E. coli cell envelope is analyzed this way, we identify and quantify 1209 unique proteins, of which 591 are predicted to be directly membrane integrated.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: 4911 binary interactions were predicted from the 1209 proteins identified in the peptidisc library.
source: From these 1209 proteins, we predict 4911 binary interactions - each characterized by a degree of precision.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by computational analysis of the data.

claim: Large membrane protein complexes are better preserved in the peptidisc workflow compared to SMA polymer.
source: We also compare the peptidisc-reconstituted membrane proteome against a membrane proteome prepared using the SMA polymer instead of detergent. We find, however, that large membrane protein complexes are better preserved in the peptidisc workflow.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by comparative experimental data.

claim: SecY associates with the membrane chaperones YfgM and PpiD.
source: With the Sec translocon, we validate association of SecY with the membrane chaperones YfgM and PpiD.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental validation.

claim: The interaction between SecY and YfgM/PpiD can be isolated in detergent only when all subunits are simultaneously over-produced.
source: This interaction can be isolated in detergent but only when all subunits are simultaneously over-produced.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: There is significant correlation between certain subunits of Sec and Bam complexes.
source: Remarkably, we also discover significant correlation between certain subunits of Sec and Bam complexes, suggesting an astonishing network of protein associations spanning across the entire bacterial cell envelope.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by correlation analysis of the data.

claim: The Bam-Sec super-complex was confirmed using SILAC AP/MS.
source: We confirm this observation using SILAC AP/MS, thereby providing direct evidence for the Bam-Sec super-complex.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental validation.

claim: All five subunits of the Bam complex are captured in peptidisc.
source: Continuing with the Bam complex, we show that all five subunits are captured in peptidisc in addition to two other interactors - RcsF and OmpA.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: RcsF and OmpA interactions with BamA were previously inferred from genetic and indirect cross-linking experiments, but direct association was not formally demonstrated.
source: These interactions were previously inferred from genetic and indirect cross-linking experiments, but direct association was not formally demonstrated (Hart et al., 2019; Konovalova et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: RcsF and OmpA interactions with BamA are much less apparent in detergent.
source: Accordingly, these interactions are much less apparent in detergent.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by comparative experimental data.

claim: Binding of the substrate binding protein MetQ to MetNI depends on its N-terminal lipidation.
source: Finally, with the ABC transporter MetNI, we find that binding of the substrate binding protein MetQ depends on its N-terminal lipidation
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: The importance of the MetQ lipid anchor is novel and is a unique case among Type I ABC transporters.
source: The importance of the MetQ lipid anchor is novel and is unique case among Type I ABC transporters.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings and comparison with other Type I ABC transporters.

claim: Most proteins perform their functions by interacting with others to achieve their full biological activity.
source: While many perform their functions independently, the majority of proteins interact with others to achieve their full biological activity.
evidence: This is a general principle in biology supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: DDM was the best detergent for extraction of the marker protein MsbA.
source: Visual analysis indicated that most, if not all, of the proteins solubilized in detergent were present in the peptidisc library (Figure 2A). However, the best extraction of the marker protein MsbA was seen with DDM; therefore, this detergent was employed in the subsequent extraction studies.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Most, if not all, of the proteins solubilized in detergent were present in the peptidisc library.
source: Visual analysis indicated that most, if not all, of the proteins solubilized in detergent were present in the peptidisc library (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by SDS-PAGE analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A total of 125 proteins and 162 proteins were identified from the detergent and peptidisc samples respectively, with ~85% overlap between the two.
source: A total of 125 proteins and 162 proteins were identified from the detergent and peptidisc samples with ~85% overlap between the two, respectively (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: His-tagged MsbA is efficiently isolated from the peptidisc library via Ni-NTA pulldown.
source: Analysis by SDS-PAGE revealed that his-tagged MsbA is efficiently isolated from the peptidisc library preparation (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Purified MsbA from peptidisc library is homogenous as shown by native PAGE analysis.
source: Native PAGE analysis revealed that the purified MsbA is, as expected, homogenous (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Individual membrane proteins are efficiently trapped in discrete peptidiscs.
source: These results strongly indicate that individual membrane proteins are efficiently trapped in discrete peptidiscs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the MsbA purification experiments.

claim: Two biological replicates were performed, resulting in the identification of 1209 proteins across the 54 fractions.
source: Two biological replicates were performed, resulting in the identification of 1209 proteins across the 54 fractions (raw data presented in Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: 591 proteins identified in the peptidisc library are predicted to be associated with the cell envelope.
source: As expected, a large fraction of these proteins (591 proteins) are predicted to be associated with the cell envelope (Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: Large assemblies such as the ribosome or GroEL complex are prone to co-sedimenting with the cell membrane fraction during ultracentrifugation.
source: Previous reports have shown that these large assemblies are prone to co‐sedimenting with the cell membrane fraction during the ultracentrifugation step after cell lysis, thus explaining their presence in our peptidisc library preparations (Papanastasiou et al., 2013; Papanastasiou et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: 1576 proteins were identified across 54 fractions from the SMALPs library.
source: Following SEC fractionation of the SMALPs library and MS analysis, we identified 1576 proteins across 54 fractions (raw data presented in Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: 705 proteins identified in the SMALPs library were predicted to be associated with the cell envelope.
source: There was good reproducibility between replicates and a large part of the identified proteins (705 proteins) was predicted to be associated with the cell envelope.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by gene ontology analysis.

claim: 1026 proteins were shared between the SMALPs and peptidisc libraries.
source: The overlap in protein content between the SMALPs and peptidisc library was excellent, with 1026 proteins shared between the two libraries.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by comparative analysis of the datasets.

claim: The overall distribution of proteins in SMALPs and peptidisc libraries, as classified according to their gene ontology annotations and originating compartment, was nearly identical.
source: Furthermore, the overall distribution of proteins in each library, as classified according to their gene ontology annotations and their originating compartment, was nearly identical (Figure 3A and Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: SMALPs and peptidiscs are both suitable for solubilization and detergent-free fractionation of the E. coli cell membrane.
source: Thus, SMALPs and peptidiscs are both suitable for solubilization and detergent-free fractionation of the E. coli cell membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparative analysis of the two methods.

claim: Detergent solubilization followed by immediate reconstitution into peptidisc results in comparable capture efficiency of the membrane proteome as direct solubilization in the SMA polymer.
source: Importantly, the similar repertoire of proteins identified in both the SMALPs and peptidiscs libraries indicate that detergent solubilization followed by immediate reconstitution into peptidisc results in comparable capture efficiency of the membrane proteome as direct solubilization in the SMA polymer.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparative analysis of protein identification in both methods.

claim: The ATP synthase complex was dissociated in the SMALPs library, causing its protein subunits to elute separately.
source: In the SMALPs library, the ATP synthase complex was dissociated, causing its protein subunits to elute separately (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by co-fractionation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The ATP synthase was preserved in peptidiscs.
source: In contrast, the ATP synthase was preserved in peptidiscs (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by co-fractionation data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The Bam complex was solubilized with the SMA polymer, but the elution profiles for the individual subunits showed weak correlation, suggesting at least partial dissociation of the complex.
source: The Bam complex (BamABCDE) was solubilized with the SMA polymer, but here the elution profiles for the individual subunits showed weak correlation, suggesting at least partial dissociation of the complex (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by co-fractionation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Each Bam subunit presented an almost identical co-fractionation pattern in peptidisc.
source: In contrast, each Bam subunit presented an almost identical co-fractionation pattern in peptidisc (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by co-fractionation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The individual subunits of the respiratory chain complex (NuoABCDGI) showed a higher degree of correlation in their fractionation profiles in peptidisc versus SMALPs.
source: Similarly, the individual subunits of the respiratory chain complex (NuoABCDGI) showed a higher degree of correlation in their fractionation profiles in peptidisc versus SMALPs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and C).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by co-fractionation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: While SMA is an effective solubilization agent, it does not stabilize large membrane protein assemblies.
source: These results indicate that while SMA is an effective solubilization agent, it does not stabilize large membrane protein assemblies.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparative analysis of complex stability in SMALPs versus peptidiscs.

claim: The peptidisc is better suited for stabilization of large, multiprotein complexes compared to SMA.
source: The peptidisc is therefore better suited for stabilization of large, multiprotein complexes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparative analysis of complex stability.

claim: Binary protein interactions in the peptidisc library were predicted using PrInCE (Predicting Interactomes via Co-Elution).
source: Binary protein interactions in the peptidisc library were predicted using PrInCE (Predicting Interactomes via Co-Elution), a software designed for analyzing PCP-SILAC datasets (Stacey et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the computational method used, supported by a citation.

claim: The predicted list of 4911 pairwise interactions captures the majority of gold standard pairwise interactions (recall = 0.80).
source: The predicted list also captures the majority of gold standard pairwise interactions (recall = 0.80, Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational validation shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Protein pairs in the predicted peptidisc interactome had well-correlated co-fractionation profiles (average R = 0.78 vs R = 0.16 for non-interacting pairs).
source: These interactions were between protein pairs with well-correlated co-fractionation profiles (average R = 0.78 vs R = 0.16, respectively; Pearson correlation).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis of the data.

claim: 824 High Confidence interactions were detected by three independent experiments in two laboratories.
source: These High Confidence interactions were detected by three independent experiments in two laboratories.
evidence: This describes the validation approach for the High Confidence subset.

claim: 824 interactions from the predicted peptidisc interactome list are also present in the two validating interactomes.
source: From the predicted peptidisc interactome list (4911 interactions), we identified 824 interactions also present in the two validating interactomes ('High Confidence' subset, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational validation.

claim: The extent of overlap between the peptidisc interactome and validating interactomes is significantly greater than the number of overlapping interactions expected by chance (p<0.001).
source: The extent of overlap is significantly greater than the number of overlapping interactions expected by chance (p<0.001, permutation test, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from statistical analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The predicted peptidisc interactome has greater overlap with the co-fractionation validating interactome than the AP/MS validating interactome.
source: Consistent with the fact that high-throughput techniques are often biased toward detecting certain protein complexes over others (Stacey et al., 2018), our predicted peptidisc interactome has greater overlap with the co-fractionation validating interactome than the AP/MS validating interactome, although both overlaps are significant (N = 2382 and 1623, respectively, p<0.001 and p<0.001, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational validation shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: The peptidisc interactome is enriched for shared gene ontology terms compared to random chance.
source: Using these measures of biological plausibility, we found the peptidisc interactome to be enriched compared to random chance, and as shown in Figure 5A–5C, the enrichment is significant for all three measures.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational validation shown in Figures 5A-5C.

claim: The peptidisc interactome is enriched for positively correlated stress phenotypes compared to random chance.
source: Using these measures of biological plausibility, we found the peptidisc interactome to be enriched compared to random chance, and as shown in Figure 5A–5C, the enrichment is significant for all three measures.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational validation shown in Figures 5A-5C.

claim: The peptidisc interactome is enriched for shared binding domains compared to random chance.
source: Using these measures of biological plausibility, we found the peptidisc interactome to be enriched compared to random chance, and as shown in Figure 5A–5C, the enrichment is significant for all three measures.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational validation shown in Figures 5A-5C.

claim: The peptidisc interactome tended to be more enriched than the CE interactome for GO terms (z = 15.6 vs z = 14.2).
source: Converting these measures to z-score, that is measuring relative to randomly rewired networks, our peptidisc interactome tended to be more enriched than the CE interactome (GO: z = 15.6 vs z = 14.2, peptidisc vs CE, respectively; Tolerome: z = 24.8 vs z = 6.2; 3did: z = 8.7 vs z = 6.3).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational validation comparing the peptidisc interactome to the CE interactome.

claim: The peptidisc interactome tended to be more enriched than the CE interactome for Tolerome profiles (z = 24.8 vs z = 6.2).
source: Converting these measures to z-score, that is measuring relative to randomly rewired networks, our peptidisc interactome tended to be more enriched than the CE interactome (GO: z = 15.6 vs z = 14.2, peptidisc vs CE, respectively; Tolerome: z = 24.8 vs z = 6.2; 3did: z = 8.7 vs z = 6.3).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational validation comparing the peptidisc interactome to the CE interactome.

claim: The peptidisc interactome tended to be more enriched than the CE interactome for 3did binding domains (z = 8.7 vs z = 6.3).
source: Converting these measures to z-score, that is measuring relative to randomly rewired networks, our peptidisc interactome tended to be more enriched than the CE interactome (GO: z = 15.6 vs z = 14.2, peptidisc vs CE, respectively; Tolerome: z = 24.8 vs z = 6.2; 3did: z = 8.7 vs z = 6.3).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational validation comparing the peptidisc interactome to the CE interactome.

claim: 340 interactions from the peptidisc interactome are also present in the CE interactome, a significant overlap (p<0.001).
source: Of the 4911 peptidisc interactions, 340 are also present in the CE interactome, a significant overlap (p<0.001, permutation test) (Figure 5D, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational validation shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Interactions that overlap with the CE interactome tend to be higher scoring than non-overlapping interactions (average interaction score 0.66 vs 0.62, p=5e-11).
source: As expected, interactions that overlap with the CE interactome tend to be higher scoring than non-overlapping interactions (average interaction score 0.66 vs 0.62, respectively; p=5e-11, Wilcoxon rank-sum test; Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational validation shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Protein pairs in the peptidisc interactome had better-than-random M3D expression profile correlation.
source: Finally, we confirmed that protein pairs in our peptidisc interactome had better-than-random M3D expression profile correlation (Faith et al., 2008) (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational validation shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Protein pairs in the peptidisc interactome had higher expression correlation than protein pairs in the E. coli CE interactome.
source: However, we also note that protein pairs in our peptidisc interactome had higher expression than protein pairs in the E. coli CE interactome (Babu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational validation comparing to the CE interactome.

claim: 202 complexes with a median size of five proteins were produced by the clustering algorithm.
source: This procedure produced 202 complexes with a median size of five proteins (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational clustering analysis.

claim: The 3490 pairwise interactions clustered in complexes had a significantly higher interaction score than the 1421 un-clustered interactions (mean interaction score 0.64 vs 0.59, p=3e-72).
source: This was indeed the case: the 3490 pairwise interactions clustered in complexes had a significantly higher interaction score than the 1421 un-clustered interactions (mean interaction score 0.64 vs 0.59, p=3e-72, Wilcoxon rank-sum test).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational clustering analysis.

claim: Interactions between the core SecYEG complex and the membrane-anchored periplasmic chaperones YfgM and PpiD are detected in the datalist at high (>75%) precision.
source: Principally, we aimed to confirm interactions between the core SecYEG complex and the membrane-anchored periplasmic chaperones YfgM and PpiD. These interactions are detected in our datalist at high (>75%) precision.
evidence: This is a finding from the peptidisc interactome data.

claim: The SecY-YfgM/PpiD interaction is difficult to detect in detergent, unless all subunits are simultaneously over-produced in the membrane.
source: However, this association is difficult to detect in detergent, unless all subunits are simultaneously over-produced in the membrane (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental validation shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Interactions between the SecY complex and the BamA, BamC and BamD subunits of the Bam complex are given in the datalist at high (>75%) precision.
source: We were also interested by the astonishing apparent interaction between the Sec and Bam complexes, also given in our datalist at high (>75%) precision. These include interactions between the SecY complex and the BamA, BamC and BamD subunits of the Bam complex.
evidence: This is a finding from the peptidisc interactome data.

claim: SecY is highly enriched after affinity pulldown in detergent extract.
source: Experiments with the detergent extract shows that SecY is highly enriched after affinity pulldown (Figure 6A, raw data presented in Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the AP/MS experiment shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Several ribosomal proteins are enriched in the SecY pulldown, which is not surprising given the intrinsic affinity of ribosomes for the Sec complex.
source: There is also enrichment of several ribosomal proteins, which is not surprising given the intrinsic affinity of ribosomes for the Sec complex (Rapoport et al., 2017; Park and Rapoport, 2012).
evidence: This finding is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Many known membrane-bound interactors of the SecY complex are not enriched in detergent, likely due to their dissociation during prolonged incubation with detergent.
source: However, many known membrane-bound interactors of the SecY complex are not enriched, likely due to their dissociation during the prolonged incubation with detergent.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results.

claim: In peptidisc, several ancillary subunits of the Sec translocon, including the periplasmic chaperones PpiD and YfgM, as well as the holo-translocon subunits YidC and YajC are detected.
source: Accordingly, in peptidisc, several ancillary subunits of the Sec translocon, including the periplasmic chaperones PpiD and YfgM, as well as the holo-translocon subunits YidC and YajC are detected.
evidence: This is a finding from the AP/MS experiment with peptidisc.

claim: There is strong enrichment of the porin OmpA in the SecY peptidisc pulldown.
source: There is also strong enrichment of the porin OmpA in addition to several subunits of the outer membrane Bam complex.
evidence: This is a finding from the AP/MS experiment with peptidisc.

claim: The BamB and BamC subunits are significantly enriched in the SecY peptidisc pulldown.
source: The BamB and BamC subunits in particular are significantly enriched (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a finding from the AP/MS experiment shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The peptidisc interaction datalist revealed a network of pairwise interactions between subunits of the Sec and Bam complexes.
source: Strikingly, the peptidisc interaction datalist also revealed a network of pairwise interactions between subunits of the Sec and Bam complexes.
evidence: This is a finding from the peptidisc interactome data.

claim: Interactions between SecYEG and the BamA, BamC and BamD subunits are present in the interaction list at high precision.
source: Interactions between SecYEG and the BamA, BamC and BamD subunits in particular are present in our interaction list at high precision.
evidence: This is a finding from the peptidisc interactome data.

claim: The Sec-Bam interaction has been suggested previously based on coincident detection between membrane fractionation and Western blotting.
source: This Sec-Bam interaction has been suggested previously based on coincident detection between membrane fractionation and Western blotting (Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: There is significant enrichment of the BamB and BamC subunits in the SecYEG peptidisc pulldown.
source: There is significant enrichment of the BamB and BamC subunits and these interactions are not detected when the same workflow is performed in detergent (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a finding from the AP/MS experiment shown in Figure 6.

claim: The Sec-Bam interactions are not detected when the same workflow is performed in detergent.
source: There is significant enrichment of the BamB and BamC subunits and these interactions are not detected when the same workflow is performed in detergent (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative AP/MS experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The BamA pulldown results reveal compelling enrichment of the Sec ancillary subunits YidC and YajC.
source: Here also the results reveal compelling enrichment of the Sec ancillary subunits YidC and YajC, adding another layer of evidence for a Sec-Bam interaction.
evidence: This is a finding from the AP/MS experiment with BamA as bait.

claim: The Sec-Bam interaction suggests a trans-membrane pathway for the direct transfer of proteins from the inner to outer membrane of the bacterial cell envelope.
source: This interaction is particularly intriguing - and exciting - as it suggests a trans-membrane pathway for the direct transfer of proteins from the inner to outer membrane of the bacterial cell envelope.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental findings.

claim: The interactome dataset identified the Sec ancillary subunits YidC and YajC as potential Bam interactors with high precision (>75%).
source: Our interactome dataset identified the Sec ancillary subunits YidC and YajC as potential Bam interactors with high precision (>75%), as well as the cell surface-exposed lipoprotein RcsF (Supplementary file 3, Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a finding from the peptidisc interactome data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The cell surface-exposed lipoprotein RcsF was identified as a potential BamA interactor with high precision (>75%).
source: Our interactome dataset identified the Sec ancillary subunits YidC and YajC as potential Bam interactors with high precision (>75%), as well as the cell surface-exposed lipoprotein RcsF (Supplementary file 3, Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a finding from the peptidisc interactome data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: BamC and BamD are the only subunits enriched along with BamA in detergent extract.
source: Experiments with the detergent extract shows that BamC and BamD are the only subunits enriched along with BamA (Figure 7B, raw data presented in Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the AP/MS experiment shown in Figure 7B.

claim: BamB is prone to dissociating from the rest of the Bam complex in detergent solution.
source: This finding is in agreement with an earlier study which showed that BamB is prone to dissociating from the rest of the complex in detergent solution (Gu et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: RcsF is significantly enriched in the BamA detergent pulldown.
source: The only other interactor that is significantly enriched is RcsF.
evidence: This is a finding from the AP/MS experiment with detergent.

claim: All four other subunits of the Bam complex (subunits B, C, D and E) are captured along with BamA in peptidisc.
source: In peptidisc, by contrast, all four other subunits of the Bam complex (subunits B, C, D and E) are captured along with BamA (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a finding from the AP/MS experiment shown in Figure 7C.

claim: There is significant enrichment of the Sec translocon ancillary subunits YidC and YajC in the BamA peptidisc pulldown.
source: Additionally, there is again significant enrichment of the Sec translocon ancillary subunits YidC and YajC, thereby providing additional evidence to support this potentially novel interaction.
evidence: This is a finding from the AP/MS experiment with peptidisc.

claim: The lipoprotein RcsF and the porin OmpA are significantly present in the BamA peptidisc pulldown.
source: The lipoprotein RcsF and the porin OmpA are also significantly present (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a finding from the AP/MS experiment shown in Figure 7C.

claim: BamA-OmpA interaction was not reported in the interactome datalist, probably due to the unusually broad SEC elution profile of OmpA, leading to false negative identification due to low score precision.
source: We note that BamA-OmpA interaction was not reported in our interactome datalist, probably due to the unusually broad SEC elution profile of OmpA, leading to false negative identification due to low score precision.
evidence: This is an explanation for a limitation in the interactome data.

claim: A series of recent publications have shown that OmpA is a bona fide interactor of both RcsF and BamA in the cell context.
source: However, a series of recent publications have shown that OmpA is a bona fide interactor of both RcsF and BamA in the cell context (Hart et al., 2019; Konovalova et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: The PCP profile of MetNI allowed prediction that MetQ forms a stable complex with MetNI.
source: The ABC transporter MetNI was chosen as a third validation target because its PCP profile allowed to predict that i) MetQ forms a stable complex with MetNI and ii) NlpA (lipoprotein 28) is a novel interactor of the transporter (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a prediction from the PCP data shown in Figure 8.

claim: NlpA (lipoprotein 28) is a novel interactor of the MetNI transporter.
source: The ABC transporter MetNI was chosen as a third validation target because its PCP profile allowed to predict that i) MetQ forms a stable complex with MetNI and ii) NlpA (lipoprotein 28) is a novel interactor of the transporter (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a prediction from the PCP data shown in Figure 8.

claim: The stable interaction of MetQ with MetNI is unexpected because type I ABC transporters are characterized by weak affinity to their substrate binding proteins (SBPs).
source: The stable interaction of MetQ with MetNI is unexpected because type I ABC transporters are characterized by weak affinity to their substrate binding proteins (SBPs).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about type I ABC transporters.

claim: The transporters LivFGM and HisQP co-elute separately from the SBPs LivJ, LivK, and HisJ, respectively.
source: Accordingly, the transporters LivFGM and HisQP co-elute separately from the SBPs LivJ, LivK, and HisJ, respectively (Figure 8—figure supplement 1. Raw data presented in Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The type II transporter FepC co-elutes tightly with FepB.
source: In contrast, but as expected, the type II transporter FepC co-elutes tightly with FepB (Bao and Duong, 2012; Bao and Duong, 2014; Hvorup et al., 2007; Rice et al., 2014) (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1, supported by citations.

claim: MetQ has a lipobox at the N-terminus, which is a unique case among other type I SBPs.
source: As an additional distinctive feature, we discovered the presence of lipobox at the N-terminus of MetQ, which is a unique case among other type I SBPs.
evidence: This is a novel finding from the study.

claim: The lipid modification of MetQ could explain why MetQ remains associated to MetNI in the peptidisc library.
source: This lipid modification could explain why MetQ remains associated to MetNI in the peptidisc library, and why this association has not been detected in earlier biochemical studies which employ the soluble, non-lipidated form of MetQ (Nguyen, 2016; Nguyen et al., 2018; Nguyen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental findings and supported by citations.

claim: The interaction of MetQ with MetNI is detected in both detergent and peptidisc.
source: The results reveal the interaction of MetQ with MetNI in both detergent and peptidisc (Figure 8 - raw data presented in Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the AP/MS experiments shown in Figure 8.

claim: The interaction of NlpA with MetNI is detected only in peptidisc, and not in detergent.
source: The interaction of NlpA with MetNI is, however, detected only in peptidisc, and not in detergent (Figure 8B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from the AP/MS experiments shown in Figures 8B and C.

claim: Lipidated MetQ co-elutes with MetNI but not MetQ-C23A (non-lipidated mutant).
source: The results indicate the co-elution of lipidated MetQ with MetNI but not MetQ-C23A, underscoring the importance of lipidation for this interaction (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the experiment shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: The peptidisc can entrap membrane proteins directly out of a crude detergent membrane extract.
source: In this study, we show that the peptidisc can entrap membrane proteins directly out of a crude detergent membrane extract.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study.

claim: The resulting peptidisc protein library is stable, water soluble and is amenable to biochemical fractionation and characterization by mass spectrometry.
source: The resulting protein library is stable, water soluble and is amenable to biochemical fractionation and characterization by mass spectrometry.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study.

claim: The peptidisc is less likely compared to the nanodisc to bias reconstitution toward a certain protein diameter due to its adaptability to membrane protein hydrophobic surfaces.
source: Because of its adaptability to membrane protein hydrophobic surfaces, the peptidisc is less likely compared to the nanodisc to bias reconstitution toward a certain protein diameter (Bayburt et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a comparison supported by a citation and the properties of the peptidisc.

claim: Addition of exogenous lipids is not required for peptidisc reconstitution, which simplifies the reconstitution while reducing protein aggregation caused by extra lipids.
source: Addition of exogenous lipids is also not required, which simplifies the reconstitution while reducing protein aggregation caused by extra lipids (Roy et al., 2015; Wilcox et al., 2015; Marty et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: The peptidisc self-assembly is rapid and does not require dialysis or detergent adsorbents.
source: The self-assembly is rapid and does not require dialysis or detergent adsorbents.
evidence: This is a characteristic of the peptidisc method.

claim: The relatively short exposure to surfactants in the peptidisc method is important as it minimizes detergent-mediated complex dissociation and aggregation.
source: This relative short exposure to surfactants is important as it minimizes detergent-mediated complex dissociation and aggregation.
evidence: This is an inference about the advantage of the peptidisc method.

claim: NlpA overproduction can complement a strain depleted for MetQ.
source: Earlier literature has reported that NlpA overproduction can complement a strain depleted for MetQ (Zhang et al., 2003), thereby providing a strong biological rationale to this interaction.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The peptidisc library combined with PCP-SILAC or AP/MS workflow is a promising novel approach for generating and validating high-throughput membrane protein interactomes.
source: In conclusion, the peptidisc library combined with PCP-SILAC or AP/MS workflow is a promising novel approach for generating and validating high-throughput membrane protein interactomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: Each interaction in the peptidisc interactome is given with an interaction score, a measure which has been shown to correlate with measures of biological plausibility.
source: First, each interaction is given with an interaction score (Supplementary file 3), a measure which has been shown to correlate with measures of biological plausibility (Stacey et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Further improvement of the precision to reduce the number of false positives is feasible by increasing the library fractionation, including separation over density gradient or ion exchange resins.
source: Further improvement of the precision to reduce the number of false positives is feasible by increasing the library fractionation, including for example separation over density gradient or ion exchange resins (McBride et al., 2017; Maddalo et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Increasing library fractionation can bias predicted interactions toward protein pairs that are already supported in the literature at the expense of detecting novel interactions.
source: However, this practice can also bias predicted interactions toward protein pairs that are already supported in the literature at the expense of detecting novel interactions.
evidence: This is a consideration about the trade-offs in methodology.

claim: The peptidisc workflow can be expanded to comparative analysis of membrane interactomes using a third amino acid isotopologue label.
source: Looking forward, the peptidisc workflow can also be expanded to comparative analysis of membrane interactomes using a third amino acid isotopologue label.
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications of the method.

claim: Using a third isotopologue label would allow profiling the changes in the global membrane protein interaction landscape under different conditions or in response to drugs and mutations.
source: This labeling would allow profiling the changes in the global membrane protein interaction landscape under different conditions or in response to drugs and mutations.
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications of the method.
